name: Pharyngeal Musculature, Fascial Spaces and Waldeyer Tonsillar Ring

reference.source: ALGrawany Anatomy & Physiology Made Easy 2026 / Scott-Brown's Otorhinolaryngology
clinicalPearls: Pharynx is divided into nasopharynx (skull base to palate), oropharynx, and laryngopharynx (down to C6 cricoid)
All pharyngeal muscles are innervated by CN X (vagus), except stylopharyngeus, which is supplied by CN IX
Killian dehiscence is a muscular gap between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus where Zenker diverticulum forms
Waldeyer ring consists of adenoid, tubal tonsils, palatine tonsils, and lingual tonsil
Retropharyngeal space lies between buccopharyngeal fascia and alar fascia, extending into posterior mediastinum
reference.pathophysiology: The pharyngeal constrictors coordinate peristaltic deglutition. Incoordination of cricopharyngeal relaxation generates high hypopharyngeal pressures, herniating posterior mucosa through Killian dehiscence. Deep cervical fascial planes encase the pharynx; infections in the retropharyngeal or danger spaces can track inferiorly into the posterior mediastinum, causing acute mediastinitis.
additionalDifferentials: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx
additionalInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced neck CT to evaluate deep neck space infections and abscesses
